title: I texted the cat from the phone I already had
body:
I did not install a new chat app. I texted from iMessage. Plow Chat is the line: a named slot on my account, Willow or whichever one was free, and the name in the dashboard is the same number I wrote.

One message in. The cat answered in the thread. Same phone, a different job whenever I asked for one.

title: Spec the signup drop-off before anyone writes code
body:
I told the cat the signup drop-off was the actual bug, and to spec it before anyone wrote code.

It opened one playbook, to-spec, and stopped at the spec. Implementation waited until I said build. No invented process, no surprise pull request.

title: Draft the cold email. Don't send it.
body:
Three design partners, one cold email, and I said don't send it.

The cat ran prospecting, then cold-email, and left a draft in the thread. Nothing went out. Sending was still my line to say.

title: Review the PR. Don't run the fork.
body:
PR 12 needed a read, not a surprise execution.

I said don't run the fork. The cat opened change-review and stayed read-only. Tests that would run untrusted code waited until I said they could.

title: Check the citations before I trust the draft
body:
I had a draft and I did not want a confident paragraph with a broken citation.

The cat opened the academic pack, checked the references, and labeled what it had actually read. A paper is a paper. It did not turn the draft into a security hunt.

title: I tapped yes before it touched my machine
body:
The cat already works from the text thread. I wanted a pause before an action hit my computer, so I opened Cat Paw Latch.

I saw the command. I tapped yes. That stop is optional. The thread still answers when the desktop app is closed.
